the conclusions in Cochrane reviews were not consistent when we applied different criteria to determine levels of "evidence."

the conclusions of Cochranes reviews of low back pain interventions vary markedly according to the rules used for determining "levels of evidence."

The main takeaway from our work is that
the rules used for pooling data from randomized clinical trials in meta-analyses have a major influence on the conclusions that are reached.
the conclusions of systematic reviews of the effects of treatments on health outcomes can vary markedly depending on the criteria for assessing the quality of evidence.
the conclusions of systematic reviews are sensitive to the rules used to assign levels of evidence to studies.
